title: Border styles, widths, colours, radius
learningObjectives: Explain border styles, widths, colours, radius and use the relevant CSS properties appropriately.

understand.concept: The border properties control the style, thickness, colour, and corner shape of an element's border. The border shorthand can set width, style, and colour together. A border style such as solid is required for a visible border in common cases.
understand.whyItMatters: Borders define component boundaries and can communicate grouping. Keep borders consistent and ensure they do not obscure content or reduce the usable space unexpectedly.
understand.analogy: A border is the frame around a card; its thickness, pattern, and colour affect how strongly the frame stands out.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps visualise the effect; CSS rendering and stacking follow browser layout and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The card has a two-pixel solid border and rounded corners. Change the border style and radius.

examples.explanation: The card has a two-pixel solid border and rounded corners. Change the border style and radius.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the relevant border, shadow, image-fit, or visual-effect behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create three cards using solid, dashed, and dotted borders. Set different corner radii.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component that uses this visual treatment without reducing readability or keyboard usability.
hints: Inspect the rendered result against different backgrounds.
Change one property at a time.
Keep focus indicators visible and content readable.

questions.prompt: Which border property is needed to make a border visible?
questions.explanation: A border generally needs a non-none style to be painted.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when adding decorative visual effects?
options: Only whether the effect looks fashionable
Whether the effect hides focus outlines
questions.explanation: Visual effects should not make content or interactive states harder to perceive.
